label: All data is synthetic and describes no real campus.

findings.title: No crossover was observed
findings.text: At a matched tolerance of 1e-8 the GPU was slower at all seven single-period network sizes, from 15.9 times the CPU time on the demo campus to 1.69 times at 800 junctions.

findings.title: The GPU median was lower at T = 720, with one failed repeat
findings.text: At T = 720 the GPU median was 41.8 s against 88.2 s on the CPU, but one of five GPU repeats stopped at the iteration limit. The GPU was slower at T = 24 and T = 168.

findings.title: GPU iteration counts vary between identical runs
findings.text: At T = 720 the GPU took between 127 and 1000 iterations on identical input. The CPU took the same number every time.

findings.title: Default GPU runs often stop at a looser tolerance
findings.text: With default settings the GPU often stopped at the acceptable level while the CPU reached 1e-8, so default times are not like for like.

findings.title: The GPU regularizes on most iterations
findings.text: With default settings the GPU applied inertia regularization on 91% of iterations on the demo campus, against 12% on the CPU. The cause was not isolated.

findings.title: Time to first solve is longer on the GPU
findings.text: A fresh process took 82.8 s on the GPU and 18.4 s on the CPU to finish its first two demo campus solves.

not_run.item: Augmented KKT system on the GPU

roadmap.needs: Reliable GPU convergence at T = 8,760, steadier iteration counts, and a factorization that fits in GPU memory.
Scenarios that share one sparsity pattern, and convergence of each scenario without manual restarts.
GPU convergence on the longer records the CPU solves, within GPU memory.
Models that ExaModels can evaluate on the GPU, and function evaluation becoming a large share of solve time.
